subChunks.title: Portfolio-Ready Patterns
subChunks.hookHtml: You know the utilities, the config, the tooling, the accessibility, the JIT scanner. Now assemble them into the patterns that appear on every portfolio and job-application project — the UI shapes that hiring managers and tech leads evaluate when looking at your work.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "Every product is a recombination of a handful of patterns. A hero section. A responsive nav. A card grid. A modal. A footer. Master these and you can scaffold any new screen in an afternoon."

Pattern 1: Responsive Navigation (fixed, glass morphism)

<nav class="fixed top-0 inset-x-0 z-50 bg-white/80 backdrop-blur-md border-b border-gray-100">
  <div class="container mx-auto px-4 h-16 flex items-center justify-between">
    <a href="/" class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-900 tracking-tight">Logo</a>

    <!-- Desktop links: hidden on mobile, flex on md+ -->
    <div class="hidden md:flex items-center gap-8">
      <a href="/about" class="text-sm text-gray-600 hover:text-gray-900 transition-colors">About</a>
      <a href="/contact" class="text-sm font-medium px-4 py-1.5 bg-gray-900 text-white rounded-full hover:bg-gray-700 transition-colors">Contact</a>
    </div>

    <!-- Mobile button: visible on mobile, hidden on md+ -->
    <button class="md:hidden p-2 text-gray-600" aria-label="Open menu">
      <span class="sr-only">Open menu</span>
    </button>
  </div>
</nav>

Pattern 2: Hero Section

<section class="min-h-screen flex items-center bg-gradient-to-br from-slate-900 to-slate-800 px-4">
  <div class="container mx-auto text-center">
    <span class="inline-flex items-center px-3 py-1 bg-blue-500/20 text-blue-400 rounded-full text-sm font-medium mb-6">
      Available for hire
    </span>
    <h1 class="text-5xl md:text-7xl font-bold text-white mb-6 tracking-tight">
      Full-Stack Developer
    </h1>
    <div class="flex gap-4 justify-center flex-wrap">
      <a class="px-8 py-4 bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500 text-white font-semibold rounded-lg transition-colors">View Work</a>
      <a class="px-8 py-4 bg-white/10 hover:bg-white/20 text-white font-semibold rounded-lg border border-white/20">Get in Touch</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

Pattern 3: Project Card with group hover

<article class="bg-white rounded-xl overflow-hidden shadow-sm hover:shadow-md transition-shadow group">
  <div class="aspect-video overflow-hidden">
    <img class="w-full h-full object-cover group-hover:scale-105 transition-transform duration-300" />
  </div>
  <div class="p-6">
    <h3 class="text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900 mb-2">Project Name</h3>
    <a class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-600 hover:text-blue-700">View project</a>
  </div>
</article>

How to approach a new portfolio project

  1. Start mobile-first. Design for the smallest breakpoint first.
  2. Establish type hierarchy first. Decide h1 (text-5xl), h2 (text-3xl), h3 (text-xl), body (text-base) before writing other classes.
  3. Pick one accent colour, three shades. light/100 for backgrounds, mid/600 for text, dark/900 for high-contrast.
  4. Use container mx-auto px-4 on every section wrapper.
  5. Add transition-* from day one. Retrofitting animations is painful.
  6. Use group + group-hover: for card hover effects.

Solomon: "You are no longer an apprentice. You have the constitution, the grammar, the habits, and the patterns. You may build now."

storyBeats.text: Solomon leads you out onto the balcony above the Pattern Gardens. The evening air is cool. Below, you can see the shapes of every screen you've built arranged like specimens.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a portfolio hero section. Apply these classes exactly:

  • .hero-section: min-h-screen, flex, items-center, justify-center, bg-gradient-to-br, from-slate-900, to-slate-800, px-4
  • .hero-inner: text-center, max-w-3xl, mx-auto
  • .hero-badge: inline-flex, items-center, px-3, py-1, bg-blue-500/20, text-blue-400, rounded-full, text-sm, font-medium, mb-6
  • .hero-title: text-5xl, font-bold, text-white, mb-6, tracking-tight
  • .hero-subtitle: text-xl, text-slate-400, mb-8, leading-relaxed, max-w-xl, mx-auto
  • .hero-cta-primary: px-8, py-4, bg-blue-600, hover:bg-blue-500, text-white, font-semibold, rounded-lg, transition-colors
  • .hero-cta-secondary: px-8, py-4, bg-white/10, hover:bg-white/20, text-white, font-semibold, rounded-lg, transition-colors, border, border-white/20

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a team member card from scratch using group / group-hover:. The card shows a photo placeholder and a name by default. On hover, a bio overlay slides up from the bottom using translate-y transitions.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through the group + group-hover: pattern for a project card that scales its image on hover. Why does this pattern work, and what alternative (and worse) approach might a junior developer reach for instead?

questions.prompt: Which pair of classes creates a fixed navbar that has a frosted-glass effect over content below it?
questions.explanation: fixed top-0 inset-x-0 pins the nav to the top of the viewport spanning full width. bg-white/80 makes it 80% opaque. backdrop-blur-md blurs the content visible through it — the frosted glass effect.

questions.prompt: You have a project card where hovering the card should scale the card image. Which pattern correctly applies the scale only to the image, triggered by hovering the card?
options: Add class 'group' to the card, then 'group-hover:scale-105 transition-transform' to the image
Add 'hover:scale-105' to both the card and the image
Add 'hover:*:scale-105' to the card to target all children
Use JavaScript to add 'scale-105' to the image on card mouseenter
questions.answer: Add class 'group' to the card, then 'group-hover:scale-105 transition-transform' to the image
questions.explanation: The group class marks the parent. Any descendant with a group-hover: prefix applies that utility when the group ancestor is hovered. This keeps the hover trigger and the visual response cleanly separated without JavaScript.

questions.prompt: A junior developer's portfolio hero text is 72px and overflows on mobile (375px). What underlying principle did they miss when building it?
options: Mobile-first: the base (unprefixed) utility is for the smallest screen — start with text-4xl and add md:text-5xl lg:text-7xl
They should use fluid typography: text-[clamp(2rem,8vw,4.5rem)] instead of responsive prefixes
The issue is fixed with max-sm:text-4xl to reduce the size on small screens
Responsive font sizes don't work with text-* utilities — use the font-size CSS property directly
questions.answer: Mobile-first: the base (unprefixed) utility is for the smallest screen — start with text-4xl and add md:text-5xl lg:text-7xl
questions.explanation: There is no Tailwind equivalent of a max-sm: prefix to decrease font size at small screens (it exists but is rarely idiomatic). The correct pattern is always to set the smallest-screen value as the base and override upward. Mobile-first means the base is the smallest. Larger screens add, never subtract.
